\begin{proof}
Set $L=H\cap K$. Since $H$ and $K$ are subgroups of $G$, $L$ is a subgroup of $G$. Let $g\in G$. Conjugation by $g$ is a bijection on $G$, and hence it preserves intersections. Therefore
\[
gLg^{-1}=g(H\cap K)g^{-1}=(gHg^{-1})\cap(gKg^{-1}).
\]
Since $H\unlhd G$ and $K\unlhd G$, we have $gHg^{-1}=H$ and $gKg^{-1}=K$. Thus
\[
gLg^{-1}=H\cap K=L.
\]
As this holds for every $g\in G$, $L\unlhd G$. Hence $H\cap K\unlhd G$.
\end{proof}
